newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends off sharply as cash trade slows.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends off sharply as cash trade slows.

text.p: Reports that cash trade slowed after gains early in the week prompted long liquidation and profit-taking in CME lumber futures, which ended sharply lower, traders said.
Lumber closed $9.40 to $3.90 per tbf lower with March off $9.30 at $426.40 and May off most at $387.80 per tbf. March and May touched limit down of $10.00 per tbf at one time.

Lack of demand and general selling was evident from the start despite a higher cash spruce quote. Cash trade became light late in the week and the forecast for the return of winter weather in the east prompted weaker ideas, they said.

Retail demand has been good the past couple of days on improving weather, and higher cash prices were put into the futures market. But interest for wood will drop again if weather cuts construction, they said.
"Every time we had a cold spell there (Northeast) the lumber prices backed off," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $413 per tbf, up $10 from Wednesday and up $17 from last Friday. They said that improving weather conditions, especially in the East, had offset the weak home building trend seen in December.
